title: Veterinary Social Workers
copy: Support for treatment decisions, caregiver strain, family conversations, grief, and communication with the veterinary team.
questions: Who is eligible for support?
Is help limited to hospital clients?
Can you help with family or child conversations?
redFlags: Caregiver strain is affecting daily life

title: Animal Chaplains & Doulas
copy: Non-medical emotional, spiritual, ritual, and planning support before, during, or after a pet's death.
questions: What training and scope do you have?
How do you work with the veterinarian?
What support do you provide on the day of goodbye?
redFlags: Medical advice is offered without a veterinary license
The veterinarian is excluded from medical decisions

title: Financial Assistance
copy: Nonprofit grants, urgent-care funds, and planning resources that may help with eligible veterinary bills.
questions: What expenses are eligible?
Must the veterinarian apply?
How quickly is a decision made?
redFlags: Payment is requested to apply for a grant
Personal financial details are requested outside a secure form
Urgent care is delayed while waiting for funding

title: Oncology & Internal Medicine
copy: Board-certified specialty care for cancer, complex chronic disease, cardiology, neurology, and internal-medicine questions.
questions: What specialty is board certified?
What records and tests are needed before the visit?
How will this team coordinate with our primary veterinarian?
redFlags: A complex diagnosis without a coordinated plan

title: In-Home Care & Pet Sitters
copy: Insured in-home help for medication routines, mobility support, bathroom breaks, and caregiver respite.
questions: Are you insured and background checked?
Can you follow written medication instructions?
What happens if my dog becomes distressed or cannot stand?
redFlags: References or insurance cannot be confirmed

title: Clinical Trials
copy: University and specialty-hospital studies for eligible dogs with cancer, arthritis, cognitive change, and other conditions.
questions: What is experimental versus standard care?
What costs or visits are required?
Can we withdraw without losing normal care?
redFlags: Standard care must be stopped without a clear reason

title: Poison Control
copy: Veterinary toxicology hotlines for suspected medication, food, plant, chemical, or household-product exposure.
questions: What product and amount may have been swallowed?
When did exposure happen?
Should we go directly to an emergency hospital?
redFlags: Do not induce vomiting unless a veterinary professional tells you to

title: Specialty Hospitals
copy: Referral hospitals with services such as surgery, neurology, cardiology, oncology, critical care, and advanced imaging.
questions: Which specialty should review the case first?
Is a referral required?
Are emergency and specialty teams in the same hospital?
redFlags: Advanced imaging or surgery may be needed
